public_rationale: On the plain reading that Google’s AI coding was confined to comments and tests, the claim is contradicted. Google’s July 2024 engineering account documents landed AI-authored changes to functional Google Ads code during an identifier migration. This does not establish that most AI-generated code was high-value or that AI designed major systems. A broader claim that much of the work was routine would remain unsettled.
limitations: The evidence is a company engineering disclosure, not an independent audit.
The result depends on reading just as confinement rather than predominantly.
Code migration is substantive maintenance, not proof of autonomous feature design.
The report establishes the state documented in July but does not date each individual code change.

our_interpretation: This is a tentative factual belief about Google’s actual internal use, rather than merely an unanswered question.
The plain reading of just is that the relevant AI coding use is confined to comments and tests, excluding substantive changes to functional product code.
The conversations explain the belief’s basis; they are not a conditional antecedent that must occur before assessment.
I use July–September 2024, the latest completed reporting quarter before the post’s discussion of Google’s code share.
Substantive maintenance of functional product code counts against the confinement claim. It need not amount to autonomous product design.

criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented Google internal deployment in the target period shows AI-generated changes to functional product code beyond comments and tests.
